vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: quickintel-scan
Version: 1.0.5

The skill facilitates a paid token security scan, requiring the agent to initiate a real-world financial transaction ($0.03 USDC) by signing a blockchain transaction. While the SKILL.md documentation is highly transparent about this payment mechanism and explicitly warns users against sharing private keys, the act of an AI agent initiating financial transactions is a high-risk capability. Furthermore, the code examples in SKILL.md demonstrate wallet integration using `process.env.PRIVATE_KEY`, which, in an agent execution environment, highlights a potential vulnerability if sensitive keys are not handled with robust security measures, even if the intent is not malicious. The extensive documentation also presents a large surface area for potential prompt injection, though no malicious instructions were detected.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only wrapper that describes how to call a paid Quick Intel contract-audit endpoint (x402 payment flow) and does not request credentials, install code, or perform unrelated actions — its declared requirements align with its purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (token security scanner) match the instructions: SKILL.md explains how to request a contract scan from Quick Intel and how the x402 payment flow works. The skill asks for no unrelated credentials, binaries, or installs — everything requested is proportional to a read-only scanning helper.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions are lengthy but remain focused: call POST https://x402.quickintel.io/v1/scan/full, handle 402 payment-required responses, and obtain a $0.03 USDC payment authorization via a wallet. The doc explicitly warns not to paste private keys and limits required input to token address + chain. Note: the runtime model cannot itself sign wallet payments — the instructions implicitly expect the human (or a connected wallet UI) to sign the payment; be cautious about any guidance that could encourage pasting sensitive secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files (instruction-only). Nothing is downloaded or written to disk by the skill itself, which is the lowest-risk install profile.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, no primary credential, and no config paths. The x402 payment scheme requires a wallet signature from the user, which is appropriate for a paid scan service and does not require the skill to hold secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent system-wide privileges or attempt to modify other skills. It does not ask to store credentials or change agent configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and focused, but take these precautions before using it: 1) Do not paste private keys, seed phrases, or wallet JSON into any prompt — the service only needs a token contract address and chain. 2) Verify the endpoint and company independently (check quickintel.io and the domain x402.quickintel.io) to avoid phishing. 3) Use a wallet you control (preferably hardware or a browser extension) to sign the $0.03 USDC payment; confirm the exact payment amount, token, and chain before approving. 4) Treat scan results as one data point: cross-check on block explorers and DEX liquidity/holder distribution. 5) If the agent asks you to perform actions that involve pasting signed messages or keys into chat, stop — signing should be done in your wallet UI, not pasted into a conversation.
